Team section

Web·by @dawood_adib·2026-08-22·inspora page·original post

What it is

Team section morph: an editorial team page - giant black 'TEAM' wordmark with a live index counter (01-06); the member portrait (rendered in a grainy stipple/dither treatment) dissolves between people (Edward Hank, Marcus Chen, Julian Cross, Priya Anand, Samuel Osei...) with a pixel-noise morph, while a spec list (name, role, socials) crossfades on the right.

Media

Frame-by-frame

0-30%
Counter 01->03: portrait dissolves via stipple noise - the old face breaks into scattered dots that reform as the next face (noise threshold wipe); name + detail list swap.
30-60%
03->05: same dither dissolve; portraits are grayscale with heavy grain; counter digits roll; right list rows fade/slide.
60-100%
05->06->01 (wraps); dissolve keeps a consistent stipple density so the image never fully empties - faces morph directly through the noise field.

Build prompt

Rebuild this interaction 1:1: a team section morph - editorial team page with a giant black "TEAM" wordmark and a live index counter (01-06). The member portrait (grainy stipple/dither treatment) dissolves between people (Edward Hank, Marcus Chen, Julian Cross, Priya Anand, Samuel Osei...) with a pixel-noise morph while a spec list (name, role, socials) crossfades on the right.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Editorial layout: giant "TEAM" wordmark, index counter "01" beside it. Center/left: grayscale heavy-grain portrait. Right: spec list - name, role, social links.

## Motion spec
Pattern: auto-advancing roster (~3s per member) with a signature dissolve.
- Cycle: hold 2.2s, then dissolve 800ms to the next member.
- Dissolve: the old face breaks into scattered dots that reform as the next face - a noise-threshold wipe where pixels flip in stipple order, ease-in-out on the threshold; stipple density stays consistent throughout so the image never fully empties.
- Counter: digits roll (odometer) 200ms.
- Right list: rows fade/slide out-in (300ms).

## Calibration
- Dissolve 800ms ease-in-out on the threshold; faces morph directly through the noise field - no white flash, no full-black frame.
- Counter roll synced to the dissolve's completion.
- The grain is heavy and constant; it is the medium, not an effect layered on top.

## Reduced motion
Portraits crossfade (300ms opacity); counter swaps without rolling.

## Don't miss
- The noise-threshold dissolve (pixels flipping in noise order) is the whole identity - a crossfade is a different, lesser piece.
- Portraits must be pre-treated to grayscale stipple at matched contrast, or the morph looks uneven.
- Roster wraps 06 -> 01 seamlessly; the loop never rests.
